messages:
Marta Reyes: Heads-up — onboarding neo-1.3 (hf -> redwood converter v2.1) is producing weird chat output in our smoke tests. Many responses end with repeated <pad> tokens and sometimes the assistant output truncates mid-sentence. Not just one prompt, seen across prompt sets.

Simon K.: Can you paste the tokenizer files you used? added_tokens.json and tokenizer_config.json would help. Also which converter flags.

Marta Reyes: Pasting abbreviated added_tokens.json and tokenizer_config.json I used:

```
// added_tokens.json
[
  {"id": 0, "content": "<pad>", "type": "special"},
  {"id": 1, "content": "<unk>", "type": "special"},
  {"id": 2, "content": "<s>", "type": "special"},
  {"id": 3, "content": "</s>", "type": "special"}
]

// tokenizer_config.json (key parts)
{
  "bos_token": "<s>",
  "eos_token": "</s>",
  "unk_token": "<unk>",
  "pad_token": "<pad>",
  "special_tokens_map": {"pad_token": "<pad>"}
}
```

Converter command: `python tools/hf_to_redwood.py --model neo-1.3 --tokenizer-dir ./tokenizer --out redwood-neo-1.3`

Model-CI Bot: CI: model-onboard-smoke (neo-1.3) — 3 failed, 5 passed. Failures show trailing <pad> sequence in assistant output.

Kai Chen: Two quick suspects: 1) HF tokenizer added_tokens.json used explicit ids, but our converter ignores provided ids and remaps based on vocab order unless special_tokens_map is present and validated. 2) Quant/trim step later prunes embeddings and reindexes the vocab which can shift ids if we don't remap by token string.

Simon K.: Hmm — the added_tokens.json you pasted has explicit ids. Our older converter assumed HF's tokenizer did not set ids and assigned them. If HF file included ids, but tokenizer_config lacked `special_tokens_map` or `added_tokens` pointer, we fell back to positional remap. That can swap pad/unk if there's an off-by-one.

Ollie: Can you run `python tools/inspect_token_ids.py redwood-neo-1.3/tokenizer.json` and dump token->id for the special tokens? Also check `vocab_size` before/after quantization.

Marta Reyes: Ran inspect — before conversion:
```
"<pad>" -> 0
"<unk>" -> 1
"<s>" -> 2
"</s>" -> 3
```
After `hf_to_redwood.py` + quantize step (8-bit):
```
"<pad>" -> 1
"<unk>" -> 0
"<s>" -> 2
"</s>" -> 3
```
So pad and unk swapped. That explains why generated outputs end with `<pad>` tokens when sampling — model thinks pad is unk or vice versa, downstream decoding messy.

Kai Chen: Quantization reindexing bug confirmed in local repro — if `prune_vocab=True` and converter does an in-place reorder without tracking special token strings, the index mapping is lost. In particular, we use a vocabulary packing routine that collapses unused tokens which assumes special tokens are at the end; HF arbitrary ordering breaks it.

Simon K.: Immediate mitigation: add an id-fixup pass post-conversion that enforces special token ids by string. Suggested pseudo: 
```
for tok in ["<pad>","<unk>","<s>","</s>"]:
  if converted_tokens[tok] != declared_specials[tok]:
    swap_indices(converted_tokens[tok], declared_specials[tok])
```
But safer is to canonicalize by string and rewrite tokenizer.json to map strings -> ids we want, then reindex embeddings accordingly.

Marta Reyes: I tried a naive swap and re-ran smoke tests — trailing pads gone on 2/3 failing cases, but one test still showed truncated output mid-sentence. The trace shows token id boundary conditions at seq_length-1 where K/V cache indexing assumes EOS token id == original value. So more places assume numeric ids, not token strings.

Ollie: Long-term fix: loader should maintain a token-id remap table and the runtime must always decode/encode using token string lookups when applying fallbacks/stop sequences. We should avoid hardcoding numeric constants for BOS/EOS/PAD/UNK in runtime logic.

Simon K.: Agreed. Short term checklist I propose: 1) patch hf_to_redwood to prefer `special_tokens_map` and fall back gracefully. 2) add id-fixup pass to preserve specials before any prune/quant step. 3) add unit test that runs HF tokenizer with shuffled added_tokens and ensures roundtrip. I'll open a PR for 1+2.

Model-CI Bot: Ticket created: INFR-3421 — "token id remap during HF import causes pad/unk swap". Linked CI failures: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/neo-1.3/1234

Kai Chen: Note: quant causes more than reorder — some quant routines drop rare-token embeddings which shrinks vocab and reassigns ids. We must mark special tokens protected from pruning. Add to the converter options: `--protect-specials`.

Marta Reyes: Thanks everyone. I'll re-run full eval with `--protect-specials` and the id-fixup patch when the PR lands. Will report back with regression numbers. :thumbsup:
